wave: SECURITY -- raw-observation deduplication relied solely on a non-cryptographic 64-bit FNV-1a hash equality as a proxy for byte-identity, letting a deliberately adversarial donor repository engineer a hash collision to silently suppress evidence of a genuinely different observation
wave_title: Seventeenth generation this cycle, and a return to the security category after an extensive run of correctness fixes. A dedicated security-focused survey scoped to genuinely fresh territory (git subprocess argument handling, symlink/TOCTOU risk, the donor-quarantine shell script, and the hash-based identity scheme's own adversarial robustness) found four of five angles sound and one real, evidence-grounded gap in the fifth. This finding required weighing against an earlier, deliberate architectural decision made before this session window began (stable_id's 64-bit FNV-1a hash was previously evaluated and judged 'adequate for this system's scale, not a defect') -- resolved by choosing a narrow, low-risk mitigation that does not reopen or contradict that decision, rather than rewriting the hash algorithm itself.
priority_classification: security -- second-highest category in the standing priority order. A real, if resource-intensive, adversarial-input concern in a system whose own stated threat model is 'arbitrary real and donor repositories from the internet the operator doesn't fully trust' -- directly threatens the exact 'one extractor may not overwrite another' evidence-preservation guarantee this codebase repeatedly documents as load-bearing.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to five specific security angles across genuinely untouched territory this cycle. Its finding was independently re-verified and substantially extended before any change: confirmed stable_id's real FNV-1a-64 implementation directly, confirmed raw_observation_id()'s real seed-string construction (which fields it does and does not include) directly, independently reasoned through the practical feasibility of a birthday-bound collision attack against a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash (concluding it is realistically within reach of a moderately resourced attacker over hours, consistent with why real-world content-addressed systems use cryptographic 256-bit+ hashes, not 64-bit general-purpose ones, for adversarial contexts), and explicitly weighed this finding against the earlier, already-settled session decision that stable_id's collision resistance was 'adequate for this system's scale' -- concluding that decision addressed ACCIDENTAL collision probability at realistic operational volume, not DELIBERATE adversarial crafting, and that this finding surfaces a materially different threat model not necessarily covered by that earlier evaluation.
key_finding: raw_observation_id()'s seed string (record_id | extractor.id:version | status | evidence_refs | provenance | payload Debug-repr) is built substantially from attacker-influenced content when the input is an untrusted donor repository -- file paths, symbol/function names, and the source text driving both `content_hash`/`span` and the payload's own Debug representation. stable_id hashes this seed with a bare 64-bit FNV-1a (no salt, no cryptographic design, explicitly a fast general-purpose hash never intended for adversarial contexts). normalize_typed_records (runtime/src/normalize/mod.rs) and the identical inline logic in build_census (runtime/src/census/mod.rs) both deduplicated purely on raw_observation_id() equality -- hash equality alone, never verified against the actual observation content -- directly contradicting normalize_typed_records's own doc comment promise: dedup happens 'ONLY on an exact raw_observation_id match (a byte-identical raw observation)'. That promise was false as written: hash equality proves only hash equality, not byte-identity. A resourced attacker able to engineer two genuinely different observations (e.g. one exposing a risky pattern, one an innocuous decoy) that collide under this weak hash could cause the dedup step to silently drop one observation's evidence with zero diagnostic -- undermining the census-completeness guarantee for a system whose purpose includes auditing untrusted donor code.
verification_before_acting: Read stable_id's real, current implementation directly, confirming it is exactly a bare FNV-1a-64 with no collision hardening.
Read raw_observation_id()'s real seed-string construction directly, confirming which fields feed it and that most are attacker-influenced when the input is an untrusted donor repository.
Read both real dedup_by call sites (normalize_typed_records, build_census) directly, confirming both used hash equality alone as the comparator, with no secondary content verification.

Confirmed SemanticObservation already derives PartialEq (a real, existing capability, not something requiring new infrastructure) before designing the fix, since the mitigation's feasibility depended on this.

Explicitly reasoned through and recorded the tension with an earlier, already-settled session decision ('stable_id... adequate for this system's scale, not a defect') rather than either ignoring that prior decision or blindly overturning it -- concluded the two evaluations addressed different threat models (accidental vs. adversarial collision) and chose a mitigation (verify full equality alongside the hash) that closes the adversarial gap WITHOUT touching stable_id's algorithm/format at all, so it does not contradict, reopen, or require re-litigating that earlier architectural decision.

Reasoned explicitly that the fix is strictly MORE conservative than the prior behavior (can only prevent a merge a hash collision would have unsoundly caused, never merge two records the old hash-only check would not have) before implementing, to be confident no new failure mode could be introduced.

design_decisions.question: Rewrite stable_id to use a cryptographic hash (e.g. SHA-256), or add a secondary content check at the dedup call sites?
design_decisions.decision: Secondary content check, not an algorithm rewrite. stable_id is used pervasively throughout the entire codebase (record IDs, evidence IDs, node IDs, edge IDs, obligation IDs, diagnostic IDs) -- changing its output format would ripple through the whole system, very likely breaking numerous tests with hardcoded expected hash-string values (this generation cycle's own earlier tests already assert exact hash strings, e.g. "raw-observation:7f885d279401ccb1"), and would reopen a real, previously-made architectural decision without a correspondingly large, deliberate justification. The narrow fix (verify full struct equality alongside the hash at the two specific call sites where hash equality was being used as a SOLE identity proxy for a security-relevant dedup decision) closes exactly the gap found, with a minimal, mechanically-verifiable, strictly-more-conservative change.

design_decisions.question: How to falsify this fix given a real FNV-1a-64 collision cannot practically be constructed inside a unit test?
design_decisions.decision: Wrote a pattern-level test using a toy type with a deliberately forced hash collision (two items sharing hash=1 but different content), proving the dedup PATTERN (`hash_equal && full_equal`) the real fix mechanically applies is correct, rather than attempting to construct or fake a real FNV-1a collision. Explicitly documented in the test itself why a real collision is infeasible to construct in this context -- that infeasibility for a fast CI test is exactly what makes it a real, if resource-intensive, adversarial concern rather than something accidentally reachable. Falsified this pattern test by temporarily reverting its own local demonstration closure to hash-only comparison (not production code, since no real collision exists to revert against), confirming it would incorrectly merge the two different-content colliding items, then restored the full pattern.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Both raw-observation dedup call sites now require full struct equality in addition to hash equality before merging two observations, closing a real gap where a deliberately adversarial donor repository could engineer a 64-bit FNV-1a collision to silently suppress evidence with zero diagnostic -- without touching stable_id's algorithm, format, or any of its other many call sites throughout the codebase.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added a_dedup_comparator_requiring_both_hash_and_full_equality_never_merges_a_hash_collision, proving the dedup pattern via a toy type with a forced hash collision (since a real FNV-1a-64 collision is computationally infeasible to construct inside a unit test -- the same property that makes this a genuine adversarial concern). Falsified by temporarily reverting the test's own local demonstration closure to hash-only comparison (there being no real production collision to revert against), confirming it would incorrectly merge (count stayed at 1 instead of 2), then restored the full pattern and confirmed it correctly preserves both colliding-but-different items (count 2) while still correctly collapsing genuinely identical content (count 1).
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo fmt --all --check: clean. cargo test --workspace: 560 total (296 adapter, 5 apps/cli, 178 core, 81 runtime), 0 failed -- up from 559 (+1 new test), confirming the strictly-more-conservative change does not regress any existing dedup expectation across the whole suite. docs audit --root .atlas: gate_ready true.

implementation.code_change: runtime/src/normalize/mod.rs -- normalize_typed_records's dedup comparator changed from `a.raw_observation_id() == b.raw_observation_id()` to `a.raw_observation_id() == b.raw_observation_id() && a == b`. runtime/src/census/mod.rs -- the identical inline logic inside build_census received the same change. Added one new pattern-level test.
implementation.docs_change: NONE -- this closes a gap between already-existing, already-stated documentation (the 'byte-identical raw observation' promise) and the code's actual prior behavior; no new architectural concept introduced.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: reasoned explicitly, before implementing, that the fix is strictly more conservative than the prior behavior (can only prevent an unsound merge, never cause a new one), eliminating the need to worry about reintroducing the sort-key-coarser-than-dedup-comparator bug class this session already fixed once this cycle in the SAME two files (the obligation dedup) -- here the change moves in the opposite, always-safe direction

falsified the underlying dedup pattern via a toy type with a genuinely forced hash collision (impossible to construct for the real FNV-1a-64/SemanticObservation case within test runtime budget), explicitly documenting why a real collision could not be constructed rather than silently substituting a weaker test without acknowledgment

explicitly weighed and recorded the tension with an earlier, already-settled session decision about stable_id's adequacy, rather than either ignoring it or unilaterally overturning it without justification -- chose a mitigation that resolves the newly-identified adversarial gap without contradicting or requiring re-litigation of that prior decision

confirmed the fix does not regress any of the 559 pre-existing tests across the whole workspace, and specifically confirmed no test anywhere depended on hash-only dedup semantics that the stricter comparator would now reject

cargo test -p runtime (new test, pattern.result: FAILED as expected -- left: 1, right: 2 (the colliding-but-different items incorrectly merged)

cargo test --workspace.totals: 560 total, 0 failed (296 adapter, 5 apps/cli, 178 core, 81 runtime)

cargo run -q -p atlas-cli -- systemize -.note: real self-census run to confirm this repository's own exact_duplicates_merged count is unaffected (no accidental collision exists in this repo's own real data, as expected); result recorded in a follow-up note

recensus_scope_after_promotion: no prior CLOSED/EXTINCT conclusion depended on hash-only dedup being sufficient, so no external conclusion requires reopening -- this repository's own real self-census data has no accidental FNV-1a collisions (astronomically unlikely at this system's real operational volume, per the earlier session's own already-correct evaluation of THAT question), so this fix changes behavior only for the adversarial scenario it targets, not for any real data this repository has processed so far

the earlier session decision that stable_id's 64-bit FNV-1a hash is 'adequate for this system's scale' remains correct and unchallenged for the ACCIDENTAL-collision question it addressed; this generation's finding is a distinct, additional concern (deliberate adversarial crafting) that this narrow fix closes without needing to revisit that decision

other stable_id-derived identities throughout the codebase (record IDs, evidence IDs, node/edge IDs, obligation IDs, diagnostic IDs) were not audited for the same hash-only-equality-as-sole-proxy pattern this generation -- the survey specifically found the two SemanticObservation dedup sites vulnerable because they are DEDUP decisions (silently dropping data on a false-positive match); other stable_id uses that are simple KEY LOOKUPS (e.g. BTreeMap indexing) rather than deduplication decisions may have different risk profiles and were not in this generation's scope -- flagged as a plausible area for a future generation to check, not defaulted into now
overall_verdict: FIXED, FALSIFIED, AND VERIFIED. Both raw-observation dedup call sites now require full content equality alongside hash equality before merging, closing a real adversarial-hash-collision gap that could let a deliberately crafted donor repository silently suppress evidence with zero diagnostic -- via a narrow, strictly-more-conservative change that does not touch stable_id's algorithm and does not reopen an earlier, separately-justified architectural decision about accidental collision adequacy. Falsified via a pattern-level test with a genuinely forced (toy) hash collision, since a real FNV-1a-64 collision is computationally infeasible to construct inside a unit test -- itself the property that makes this a real, if resource-intensive, concern. Full workspace test suite green (560/560).
